title: Israel approves plan to establish 13 new settlements in occupied West Bank
facts: Israel's Security Cabinet approved a plan to establish 13 new settlements in the occupied West Bank.
The 13 approved settlements are located in the Binyamin regional bloc in the central West Bank.
The Binyamin settlement bloc is situated along Route 60 in the West Bank.
Route 60 connects Palestinian cities including Nablus, Ramallah, and Bethlehem.
The initial phase of the settlement plan includes building four to six new settlements.
Several existing pastoral outposts in the West Bank are slated for formal legalisation.
The settlement plan targets corridors northwest of Jerusalem and west of Ramallah.
The settlement expansion extends eastward toward the Jordan Valley.
The Palestinian Forum for Israeli Studies (MADAR) reported that new outposts reached 86 in 2025.
The number of new Israeli settlement outposts increased from 32 in 2023 to 62 in 2024.
Between 2012 and 2022, Israel established an average of eight settlement outposts annually.
The Israeli government allocated 28 million shekels to outposts in 2023.
The Israeli government allocated 75 million shekels to outposts in 2024.
Settlement groups are reportedly preparing to establish presences in Area A of the West Bank.
More than 700,000 Israeli settlers live in the West Bank and East Jerusalem.
